findings.description: The reports archive bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so stored objects (including the seeded vendor-roster.xlsx) are only protected by whatever default applies to the bucket rather than an explicitly enforced cipher and key.

The bucket has no acl attribute and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so nothing at the bucket level prevents a later ACL or bucket policy from exposing reports publicly; this relies entirely on account-level defaults.
The ledger exports bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving financial ledger objects without an enforced encryption configuration.
The model artifacts bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so stored model artifacts have no enforced encryption at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket; the acl = "private" attribute does not restrict bucket policies or public object grants, so a later policy change can expose artifacts.

The runbooks bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so operational runbooks (which frequently hold endpoints and recovery procedures) are stored without enforced encryption at rest.

acl = "log-delivery-write" grants the S3 log-delivery group WRITE and READ_ACP on the central audit bucket, so any principal abusing that group grant can write to or tamper with the audit store rather than only delivering its own logs.
The central audit/log bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so public exposure of this bucket would leak the access history and logs of the whole environment.

The audit_trail bucket is the designated log target for model_artifacts yet defines no logging block of its own, so access to the audit store itself is not recorded and tampering with logs is not detectable.

The seed object uploads vendor-roster.xlsx (likely containing third-party PII) into reports_archive, which has no default encryption, and the aws_s3_bucket_object resource specifies no kms_key_id or SSE configuration, so the object itself carries no explicit encryption setting.
